observed_vs_expected: Expected observations state best_target_score should rise, but it fell from 0.953150 in round 1 to 0.839125 in round 2, a lower deviation with a magnitude of ~0.114. Other expectations held: valid_candidates remained high at 9, and tightest_margin stayed positive at 0.4509. The reflectance targets at 400 nm or 700 nm were not met better, consistent with the score decline.
deviation_mechanism: The optimizer pushed several layer thicknesses well beyond the fundamental quarter-wave optical regime (expanding up to ~185 nm and ~150 nm). At visible wavelengths, such extreme deviations shift the round-trip phase accumulation beyond λ/4, exciting higher-order interference modes. This creates phase mismatches that convert constructive interference at the target bands into destructive interference, while increasing out-of-band spectral leakage. The positive tightest margin confirms the stacks remain physically fabricable, but the optical response is misaligned due to over-expansion of the optical path difference.
continue_rationale: Exactly two rounds have executed. Although the score degraded, valid_candidates=9 and tightest_margin=0.4509 prove the design space remains physically viable. The performance drop is characteristic of an optimizer overshooting into a non-fundamental resonance regime rather than hitting a hard physical or constraint boundary. Implementing a bounded initialization or step-size reduction offers clear scientific benefit to navigate back toward the primary interference optimum.
insight_for_next: Re-initialize the optimizer around the Round 1 best candidate and enforce strict thickness clamping that limits each layer to ±35% of its initial quarter-wave value. Alternatively, add a penalty term in the scoring objective for layers exceeding 130 nm to keep the stack within the fundamental interference window.
insight_grounding: Candidate 3 (the fourth list in observed_metrics.candidate_thicknesses_nm) shows layer 12 expanded to 185.0929 nm and layer 9 to 150.2910 nm. These values drastically exceed the baseline ~60–100 nm quarter-wave range. Correlating these specific thickness excursions with the measured score drop from 0.9531504284001773 (round 1) to 0.8391254100223681 (round 2) demonstrates that breaching the fundamental resonance threshold directly triggers the observed spectral degradation.
